title: Auth, Security + Testing
goal: Add users, roles and login to the booking API, and make it hard to break.
outcomes: Hash passwords and issue short-lived JWTs in httpOnly cookies
Enforce authentication vs authorization with role and ownership checks (401 vs 403)
Implement Google login (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC) safely, with state and verified-email linking
Harden an API: Helmet, CORS allowlist, rate limits, Origin checks, dependency scanning
Attack your own API (SQLi, mass assignment, IDOR) and write up the results
Run integration tests in GitHub Actions with branch protection
projectStage: Booking API v2 — adds users table, signup/login/logout/me, roles (owner, staff, customer), Google login, security middleware, CI.

days.title: Authentication
learn: Password hashing (argon2 or bcrypt), sessions vs JWT, access and refresh tokens, httpOnly cookies, token expiry
tasks: Add a users table (email with a unique index on lower(email), password_hash, role) as a migration, and link customers.user_id and staff.user_id to it.
Build POST /signup, POST /login, POST /logout and GET /me.
Issue short-lived JWTs (1 hour) in httpOnly cookies.
acceptance: Passwords are never stored or logged in plain text.
Wrong credentials return 401 with the same message for "no such user" and "wrong password".
Tokens expire. Secrets come from .env.
Emails are unique regardless of case.

days.title: Authorization + Roles
learn: Authentication vs authorization, roles (owner, staff, customer), ownership checks, permission middleware, 401 vs 403
tasks: Owners manage services and staff. Staff see their own schedule. Customers see and cancel only their own bookings.
Add a permission middleware and use it on every route.
acceptance: A customer cannot read or cancel another customer's booking (tested).
Wrong role returns 403, missing login returns 401.
Every route has an explicit permission rule.

days.title: Google Login (OAuth)
learn: How OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect work (redirect, code, token exchange, state, PKCE)
Using a maintained library on top of the Day 1 auth (Arctic, or Passport.js with passport-google-oauth20)
Linking a Google account to an existing email
tasks: Add "Sign in with Google".
Link Google login to an existing account with the same verified email. Serve a minimal confirm-password form from the API for now (Week 3 moves it into Next.js).
acceptance: Email/password and Google login both work.
The state parameter is checked (no login CSRF).
The Google client secret lives in .env only.
Linking happens only when Google reports email_verified and the user confirms their existing password.

days.title: Security Hardening
learn: OWASP Top 10 basics, Helmet, CORS allowlist, rate limiting, CSRF for cookie auth, input validation, secrets management, dependency scanning (npm audit, Semgrep)
tasks: Add Helmet, a CORS allowlist, and rate limiting on login and signup.
Add an Origin check on every state-changing route (CSRF protection for cookie auth).
Run npm audit and Semgrep. Fix or document every finding.
Attack your own API: SQL injection, mass assignment (sending role=owner on signup), IDOR (changing booking IDs in the URL).
acceptance: CORS allows the frontend origin only.
Repeated failed logins are rate-limited.
curl -X POST /bookings with a valid session cookie and an Origin header of https://evil.example returns 403.
Each attack attempt is written up with its result.

days.title: Integration Tests + CI
learn: Integration tests against a real test database, fixtures, testing auth flows, coverage reports, GitHub Actions
tasks: Write tests for signup, login, logout, roles and ownership.
Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs lint + tests on every PR (with a pgvector/pgvector:pg17 service container, the same image as local).
Turn on branch protection so PRs cannot merge when CI fails. Use a public repo (private repos need a paid plan) and turn on "Do not allow bypassing the above settings".
Ask the AI agent to refactor all routes to one consistent error format. Review the diff, run the tests and keep only verified changes.
acceptance: CI is green on main.
80%+ coverage on auth and booking logic.
A PR with a failing test is blocked from merging.

days.title: Debug Lab (no AI)
learn: Testing attacks with curl and Bruno, reading auth logs
Finding leaked secrets in Git history (git log -p, gitleaks)
brokenLab: SQL injection in the login query
Any logged-in user can cancel anyone's booking
A secret committed to Git history
tasks: Fix all five issues in the provided auth system, with tests for each fix.
acceptance: Login is secure, the SQL injection attempt fails, and expired tokens are rejected.
Users can only change their own bookings.
The leaked secret is rotated, and you can explain why deleting the file is not enough.
Tests written for each fix.
Each fix written up as: symptom → cause → fix → how verified.

days.title: Weekly Project: Booking API v2
tasks: Client message: "Staff keep seeing each other's customers, and someone cancelled a booking that wasn't theirs." Update the scope first.
Email/password + Google login.
Roles: owner, staff and customer, with ownership checks on every route.
Helmet, CORS allowlist, rate limiting, Zod validation.
Integration tests running in GitHub Actions.
Security notes in the README: what was tested and how.
acceptance: See the rubric on the Project tab.
